meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero on his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so who decided that, and when?

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. Your own procedure says you speak to the student before anything else, so was Owen heard before that zero went in?
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then put it in front of me. And I'm still waiting on whether anyone spoke to Owen first.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

I'm writing down the times: created at 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58. That tells me when text landed in that file, Hale, not who wrote it or where. Has Owen been shown this and asked to explain it?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.

"Anywhere in the history" means anywhere in that one file, and that's all it means. You've now gone past my question about whether Owen was ever asked to explain this, twice, and I'm writing that down too. What else do you have?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Put the October 15 outline next to the essay so I can read both myself. A seventeen-year-old changing his argument between an outline and a final draft is called revising, Hale. But whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.

I'm writing down that line, and I'll search the play tonight myself. A misquoted line is a mistake in an essay, Hale, not a confession. Tell me exactly what you're proposing, and how it stays private.
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Good, because he isn't one. I asked what you're proposing, and the clock on my call hasn't stopped.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
I'm reading it, September 24, written in class under a clock. Tell me what you think it proves, and then give me your terms.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Okay. To put this behind him, Owen sits the rewrite privately, not in front of his class, and its mark replaces the zero, the way your own 4.4 reads. I want "nothing goes on file" in writing from you before he sits it, and it's done well before December 1.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Ten minutes. Lunch in your room, fine. Which day, and when does the email saying nothing goes on file reach me?
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

Comfortable isn't on the table, Hale; I've already given you my terms. A date for the rewrite, the rewrite mark replacing the zero, and an email before he sits it saying nothing goes on file, with the principal copied. Name the day.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
"Tonight." I'm writing that down. That still leaves the day Owen sits it, Hale.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
The day he sits it. Everything else in that email I've already given you.
Then I'll send it by eight.
By eight tonight, noted. That email is no good to me without a date for the rewrite in it, Hale.
Thank you for coming in.
Don't thank me yet, Hale. I'm not getting up until you give me a day for that rewrite.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
"Tomorrow at lunch." To sit the rewrite, or to talk to him first, because I want that spelled out in your eight o'clock email.
